question: In October 2022 who was appointed as the presiding officer of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) tribunal by the Central government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Dinesh Kumar Sharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government has appointed **Justice Dinesh Kumar Sharma of the Delhi High Court** as the **Presiding officer of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act Tribunal**.
 
• The presiding officer has been** appointed to review the ban on the Popular Front of India (PFI) and its associates**.
 
• The center has recently banned PFI for five years, after seizing incriminating documents during the search operations at the offices of the outfit and the residences of its office bearers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, or UAPA, was initially passed by the Government of India in 1967 as a measure to tackle unlawful activities, associations, and individual actions threatening the territorial integrity and sovereignty of India.
 
• This act has been reformed and strengthened over time, particularly following its significant amendments in 2004 and 2008.
 
• The UAPA Tribunal is a body set up under this Act, primarily tasked with **adjudicating whether or not there are sufficient causes for declaring an association as "unlawful".**
 
• The **Central Government constitutes the Tribunal and appoints the presiding officer, who is a sitting Judge of a High Court**.
 
• This presiding officer is given all powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code, of Civil Procedure, and functions in the unbiased nature of a judicial organ, separate from traditionally politically motivated state forces.
